sections.title: Joash's Reign Begins
observations: Joash becomes king at a young age, illustrating God's providence in preserving the Davidic line despite the threats against it.
His reign is marked by a commitment to restoring the temple and reviving true worship in Judah, reflecting the importance of leadership in spiritual matters.

sections.title: Restoration of the Temple
observations: Joash's desire to repair the temple signifies a return to proper worship and the centrality of the temple in Israel's life.
The collection of funds for the temple repairs shows the communal responsibility of the people in supporting worship.

sections.title: The Prophetic Warning
observations: The chapter highlights the role of prophets in calling the people back to faithfulness, emphasizing the need for accountability in leadership.
Joash's initial faithfulness contrasts sharply with his later actions, serving as a warning about the dangers of turning away from God.

sections.title: The Death of Joash
observations: Joash's tragic end serves as a reminder of the consequences of abandoning God's ways, even after a period of faithfulness.
His assassination by his own officials illustrates the theme of betrayal and the fragility of human leadership.

importantVerses.commentary: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest, highlighting the importance of godly mentorship in leadership.
Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, emphasizing the role of the Holy Spirit in empowering prophetic voices to call the nation back to God.

questions: What does Joash's early faithfulness teach us about the influence of mentors in our spiritual lives?
How can we ensure that our worship remains centered on God and not on human traditions or structures?
What lessons can we learn from Joash's downfall regarding the importance of remaining steadfast in faith?
